title: Teaching
text:
Here you can find a list of the courses I taught at Paderborn University until March 2026.




Angewandte Zeitreihenanalyse und Einführung in die Finanzökonometrie


Course ID: M.184.2453


Level: Bachelor


Role: Tutor


Contents: White noise, random walks, ARMA models, GARCH models, forecasting, application with R


Course language: German





Econometrics

Course ID: M.184.4479


Level: Master


Role: Tutor


Contents: Simple and multiple linear regression, hypothesis testing, point and interval predictions, heteroskedasticity, multicollinearity


Course language: English





Financial Econometrics and Quantitative Risk Management

Course ID: M.184.4451


Level: Master


Role: Tutor

Advanced Time Series Analysis and Forecasting

Course ID: M.184.5453


Level: Master

Contents: Seasonal time series, (semiparametric) FARIMA models, VARMA models, cointegration, (semiparametric) ACD models, high-frequency time series, FIGARCH models, multivariate GARCH models, forecasting

title: Blog “Stats Rsenal”
text: Welcome to the blog Stats Rsenal. Every now and then I will upload a post here on a topic from data science, time series analysis and programming.

title: Welcome to Stats Rsenal
text:
Welcome to Stats Rsenal!
Starting a blog on data analysis with a focus on programming has been a long-time idea of mine. However, due to other obligations the realization was postponed time and time again. Nonetheless, now it is finally time to start this project and bring the joy of data analysis to the world.
On an irregular basis, I will share with you posts teaching about programming, applied statistics, machine learning, and time series analysis.
Please feel free to learn more about me on my homepage, and reach out, if you have feedback on my posts.
Stay tuned for exciting updates! With that being said, what better way is there to start such a blog than with the most popular words in the world of programming?

title: Hi everyone, I’m Dominik Schulz!
text:
Statistician & Data Scientist


I am a former PhD student and a former scientific employee at the Chair of Econometrics and Quantitative Methods, Faculty of Business Administration and Economics, Paderborn University. My training includes statistics and data science and the focus of my research so far is on time series analysis as well as the development of statistical software in this context, in particular for the free software R.
This site functions both as a personal website and a blog (called Stats Rsenal) on topics related to data science, time series analysis, and programming. However, new blog posts will only appear irregularly.
If you have any feedback or suggestions, please feel free to reach out via dominik.schulz.r@gmail.com.
